chunks: Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakoony, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "Intercourse becomes legitimate in three ways: marriage with inheritance, marriage by possession of the right hand, and marriage without inheritance."

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful; title for Imam Ali
key_terms.الْفُرُوجُ: The private parts; refers to sexual intercourse
key_terms.مَلَكُ الْيَمِينِ: Possession of the right hand; refers to slave women

ai.seo_question: What are the three ways sexual intercourse becomes legitimate in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Khisal, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) categorizes the three juridical avenues for legitimizing intimacy, reflecting the classical Shia fiqh distinction between permanent marriage, temporary marriage (mut'ah), and concubinage. The inclusion of 'marriage without inheritance' specifically points to the validity of mut'ah, a practice central to Shia jurisprudence, while 'marriage with inheritance' refers to permanent nikah. This classification underscores the comprehensive nature of Islamic law in regulating private relations through distinct contractual and possessive mechanisms.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-106 Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted his grandfather, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad (MGB) , on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB) that the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) said, “There are three ways by which having intercourse becomes legitimate. They are marriage with right to inherit , marriage by possessing the woman (who is a slave), and marriage without the right to inherit .”
